elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. Debt rose from 602.3 million to 905.8 million, with a sharp increase around the middle of the period.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type

elements.description: Linked stacked bars break down 2025 external debt into public and publicly guaranteed and short-term debt, then divide public and publicly guaranteed debt by creditor type. Multilateral creditors account for the largest creditor-type amount, 493.7 million, and private creditors the smallest, 130.4 million. World Bank-IDA is the largest named multilateral creditor at 273.4 million, while Venezuela, RB is the largest bilateral creditor at 137.8 million.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four line charts show debt ratios from 2015 to 2025 against the shaded percentile range of DRS reporting countries. In 2025, external debt / exports is the highest displayed ratio at 105%, while debt service / GNI is the lowest at 4%. The printed changes are positive for three ratios and negative for external debt / GNI.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two boxes present average terms on 2025 commitments. The Official creditors box shows maturity of 37 yrs, grace period of 9 yrs, and interest rate of 0.8%, each above a small horizontal indicator. The Private creditors box shows '..' for maturity, grace period, and interest rate, above empty indicators.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
